fix_commit_message:
Bug 2018075 - Add missing write barrier in BaseScript::swapData r=jandem

The problem here is the we have a write barrier for the data contained in the
script private data buffer allocation, but not the buffer allocation itself. We
need a better abstraction to avoid problems like in the future but for now the
patch fixes the immediate problem.

Differential Revision: https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D284238
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix e055cf04d23f on top of intro 398a31295dff via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (UseAfterFree): After migrating BaseScript's PrivateScriptData storage to use the GC BufferAllocator (Bug 2002790), BaseScript::swapData() continued to rely solely on GCStructPtr::set()'s write barrier, which only barriers the GC things referenced from within PrivateScriptData, not the buffer allocation pointer (data_) itself. Since the buffer allocation can now live in the nursery and be moved/freed independently, failing to barrier the data_ edge itself can cause the GC to lose track of (or prematurely free) the old PrivateScriptData buffer during script delazification/relazification, leading to a later use-after-free style access when the tracer walks a stale buffer pointer, producing an assertion failure (`isAllocated(alloc)`) or SEGV inside BufferAllocator code. Root cause: BaseScript::swapData/releaseData assumed that GCStructPtr::set() barriers were sufficient for updating the data_ pointer, which was true when PrivateScriptData was a plain heap allocation. Once Bug 2002790 made data_ a BufferAllocator-managed (nursery-capable) allocation, the pointer itself became a GC edge requiring its own trace/write barrier (via TraceBufferEdge), which was not added at the same time, leaving a gap between allocation-strategy change and barrier coverage.
